narrativeProgression.description: The teacher introduces the topic of electrostatic field electron acceleration.
The teacher poses the question: Why aren't electrons sucked back to the anode?
The teacher begins drawing a diagram of a cathode and anode on the whiteboard.
The teacher explains the common misconception that electrons are attracted to anodes and repelled by cathodes.
The teacher clarifies that electrons are not actually attracted or repelled by the anode and cathode directly.
The teacher introduces the concept of electrostatic field lines and how they influence electron acceleration.
The teacher draws electrostatic field lines on the whiteboard to illustrate the concept.
The teacher draws arrows to show how electrons are accelerated along the electrostatic field lines.
The teacher emphasizes that electrons are accelerated towards the positive end of the electrostatic field and repelled by the negative end.
The teacher explains that once electrons leave the electrostatic field, they are no longer accelerated by it.
